summary: The invoice-2 crisis closed - and the client closed it. On Aug 31 Lauren phoned Chase herself and came back with the root cause ALTR had spent six chase messages and sixteen days not finding: "They said that the name ALTR mgmt LLC is not matching the name on the account even though the numbers are" and, far more seriously, "And your account was flagged by Chase for fraud/scam transactions so they won’t send it through so they won’t send it even if I say so". Nobody at ALTR has responded to that second sentence to this day. Stephski's next two messages were "Thanks so much so so sorry for the difficulties!" and notice that invoice 3 was coming. Lauren then routed around the broken rail on her own: three daily Zelle payments at her $5k limit on Aug 31, Sep 1 and Sep 2 ("3/3 Zelle for last invoice"), settling invoice 2 eighteen days after issue while she was in LA and Mexico. Invoice 3 (period Aug 15-31) went out Sep 1 and she had already sent the first $5k against it by Sep 3 - and in the same message asked, for the second time, "Can you confirm the name of the account?". It took a Mayson nudge ("@stephskiii ^^") and four hours twenty minutes to get the one-line answer "The name on the account is ALTR MANAGEMENT LLC", with no corrected invoice, no routing/SWIFT or registered address, and still no acknowledgement of the fraud flag. Service delivery hit its lowest point yet. Derrek sent ZERO messages in the window, the week after sending six - every one of them a payment chase. Ollie sent two, both of them asks: a fan-follow request on Aug 30 and "Hey Lauren, where are the new pictures?" on Sep 4, four days after she wrote "Uploaded some new pics". None of his five open items moved - boundary confirmation 33 days, whale report 28, CodyBeebs screenshot 17, and the livestream he built a subscriber poll for has now gone 14 days without a single mention. Michelle delivered the weekly leak report on time and unchased on Sep 1, the seventh consecutive week and still the only service line on this account that has never needed a reminder.

health.rationale: Down 4 from 55. The acute risk did clear - invoice 2 is settled and invoice 3 is already part-paid - and that is the only reason this is not in the 40s. But look at how it cleared. The client phoned her own bank, diagnosed ALTR's beneficiary-name mismatch, discovered ALTR's account is flagged by Chase for fraud, invented the workaround, executed it over three days while travelling, and apologised to ALTR for the delay ("It’s all good sorry for the delay. I’ll get it handled today"). ALTR contributed six chases and a one-line answer that took two asks and a colleague's @-mention to extract. The fraud-flag disclosure - a bank telling a paying client that this agency's account is associated with scam transactions - was met with silence from every ALTR staff member including the owner. Meanwhile service went to zero: Derrek 0 messages, Ollie 2 and both were requests of her, and all nine stale promises got a week older. She is now on manual Zelle installments indefinitely because the wire rail still is not fixed. Her conduct this week rates a 90; ALTR's delivery rates a 25.
